title: Weighing the Cost of Constant Connectivity
paragraphs: After noticing that constant work notifications had gradually eroded his ability to fully engage with his family during evenings, Taufik began questioning whether the productivity benefits of constant connectivity genuinely outweighed its considerable personal costs.

His initial attempt to simply silence notifications entirely created anxiety about missing genuinely urgent matters, a fear that proved largely unfounded once he tested the boundary over several actual weeks.

Working with his manager, Taufik established clearer expectations about which situations genuinely warranted after-hours contact, distinguishing them explicitly from routine matters that could reasonably wait until the following workday.

Reflecting on this adjustment months later, Taufik notes that most perceived urgency had been habitual rather than genuine, and that reclaiming his evenings had improved both his family relationships and, unexpectedly, his actual work performance.
